title: A gas matches both the outline and the room inside its holder
summary: A gas takes on both the outline and the full amount of space of whatever holds it.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a gas adopts the outline of its holder and also the holder's whole interior space. A balloon is the section's proof that a gas really occupies room: with nothing in it, the balloon would stay limp. Clouds can look like one drifting body, yet the page treats a cloud as air mixed with tiny bits of water, not as one pure gas. This card stops at how a gas fills a holder. It does not state a pressure formula.

sources.note: OpenStax Chemistry, first-edition path /books/chemistry/, CC BY 4.0. Supports a gas taking both the shape and the volume of its container, and the cloud as a mixture, in section 1.2. Paraphrase only; the section was not copied.
